subtopic: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
stem: A negatively charged particle travels with a velocity \(\vec{v}\) through a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) as shown in the following figure, in three different situations. What is the direction of the magnetic force \(\vec{F}_m\) due to the magnetic field, on the particle?
solution:
In Fig. (a), \(\vec{v}\) points along the \(-x\) direction and \(\vec{B}\) along the \(-z\) direction, so
\(\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = (-\hat{x}) \times (-\hat{z}) = \hat{x} \times \hat{z} = -\hat{y}\),
i.e. \(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}\) is in the negative \(y\) direction. The particle carries a negative charge, so \(\vec{F}_m = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})\) is opposite to \(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}\). Hence \(\vec{F}_m\) will be in the positive \(y\) direction.

In Fig. (b), \(\vec{v}\) points along the \(-z\) direction and \(\vec{B}\) along the \(+y\) direction, so
\(\vec{v} \times \vec{B} = (-\hat{z}) \times \hat{y} = +\hat{x}\),
i.e. \(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}\) will be in the positive \(x\) direction. Hence the force \(\vec{F}_m\) on the negative charge will be in the opposite direction, i.e. along the negative \(x\) direction.

In Fig. (c), \(\vec{v}\) and \(\vec{B}\) are anti-parallel, the angle between them is \(180^\circ\) and because \(\sin 180^\circ = 0\), \(\vec{F}_m\) will be zero, i.e., no force acts on the particle.

subtopic: Magnetic Force on a Moving Charge
stem:
A particle of charge \(q\) follows a trajectory as shown in the figure. Obtain the type of the charge (positive or negatively charged). Obtain the momentum \(p\) of the particle in terms of \(B, L, s, q\), \(s\) being the distance travelled by the particle.

Particle trajectory: A uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) is applied in the region pp', perpendicular to the plane of the paper, coming out of the plane of the paper.
solution:
\(\vec{B}\) is coming out of the paper. Since the particle moves upwards, there must be a force in that direction. The velocity is in the positive \(x\) direction.

\(\therefore\) \(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}\) is in the \(-\)ve \(y\) direction. As the force is in \(+y\) direction, i.e., opposite, the charge must be negative.

According to Eq. (10.7), magnitude of the momentum \(p = qBR\). The trajectory is circular with radius \(R\).

Using upper triangle in the figure,
\((R - S)^2 + L^2 = R^2\)

\(\therefore R = \dfrac{S^2 + L^2}{2S}\) ;

\(p = qBR = \dfrac{qB\left(S^2 + L^2\right)}{2S}\)

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Wire
stem: Consider a square loop of wire loaded with a glass bulb of mass \(m\) hanging vertically, suspended in air with its one part in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) with its direction coming out of the plane of the paper \((\odot)\). Due to the current \(I\) flowing through the loop, there is a magnetic force in upward direction. Calculate the current \(I\) in the loop for which the magnetic force would be exactly balanced by the force on mass \(m\) due to gravity.
solution:
The current \(I\) in the loop with its part in the magnetic field \(B\) causes an upward force \(F_m\) in the horizontal part of the loop, given by

\(F_m = IBa\),

where \(a\) is the length of one arm of the loop.

This force is balanced by the force due to gravity.

\(\therefore F_m = I\,Ba = mg\)

\(\therefore I = \dfrac{mg}{Ba}\)

For this current, the wire loop will hang in air.

subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current
stem: A wire has 2 straight sections and one arc as shown in the figure. Determine the direction and magnitude of the magnetic field produced at the centre O of the semicircle by the three sections individually and the total.
solution:
We apply the Biot-Savart law to the 3 sections of the wire.

For the section (i) and (iii) the angle between the current-length elements \(I\,\mathrm{d}\vec{l}\) and \(\vec{R}\) is \(180^\circ\) and \(0^\circ\), respectively.

\(\therefore dB = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Idl \sin(180)^\circ}{R^2} = 0 = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Idl \sin(0)^\circ}{R^2}\)

For section (ii), \(\mathrm{d}\vec{l}\) is always perpendicular to \(\vec{R}\).

\(\therefore dB = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Idl \sin (90^\circ)}{R^2} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Idl}{R^2}\)

Integrating, \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{R^2}\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi R} dl = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{R^2}\pi R\)

\(\therefore B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4}\dfrac{I}{R}\)

\(\therefore\) For the sections (i), and (iii), \(B = 0\), for section (ii) \(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R}\) at the point O.

Total \(B = 0 + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R} + 0 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R}\).

Direction of \(B\): the current runs left to right and so traverses the semicircle clockwise as seen on the page (from the left end, over the top, down to the right end). For an element at the top of the arc, \(\mathrm{d}\vec{l}\) is along \(+\hat{x}\) while the unit vector from that element to O is \(-\hat{y}\), so \(\mathrm{d}\vec{l} \times \hat{r} = \hat{x} \times (-\hat{y}) = -\hat{z}\). Every element of the arc gives the same sense, so \(\vec{B}\) at O is directed INTO the plane of the paper.

subtopic: Ampere's Law, Solenoid and Toroid
stem: A coaxial cable consists of a central conducting core wire of radius \(a\) and a coaxial cylindrical outer conductor of radius \(b\) (see figure). The two conductors carry an equal current \(I\) in opposite directions in and out of the plane of the paper. What will be the magnitude of the magnetic field \(B\) for (i) \(a < r < b\) and (ii) \(b < r\)? What will be its direction?
solution:
By symmetry, \(B\) will be tangent to any circle centred on the central conductor. In order to apply the Ampere's law, consider a circle of radius \(r\) such that \(a < r < b\).

\(\therefore \displaystyle\oint \vec{B}.\mathrm{d}\vec{l} = \mu_0 I\)

\(\therefore B.2\pi r = \mu_0 I\)

\(\therefore B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}\), \(a < r < b\)

For \(r > b\),

\(\therefore \displaystyle\oint \vec{B}.\mathrm{d}\vec{l} = \mu_0 (I - I) = 0\) (\(\because\) The two currents are equal and opposite)

\(\therefore B.2\pi r = 0\), \(r > b\)

(Try to solve this using Biot-Savart Law!)

subtopic: Ampere's Law, Solenoid and Toroid
stem: A solenoid of length 25 cm has inner radius of 1 cm and is made up of 250 turns of copper wire. For a current of 3 A in it, what will be the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the solenoid?
solution:
We use Eq. (10.65)

\(B = \mu_0\, n\, i\)

\(B = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times \dfrac{250}{0.25} \times 3\)

\(B = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{3} \times 3\)

\(\therefore B = 3.77 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T}\)
